narrative.overview:
The page is the product running. A real terminal, drawn cell for cell by the app itself, sits in a graphite bezel under a soft white spotlight, and everything else on the page is quiet enough to let it be the brightest thing. The site and the CLI are one system: the site palette is the `mono` theme in `packages/tui/src/theme.ts` (ground, ink, three greys, up, down, warn), so the screen and the page read as one surface and a change to one is a change to both.

The world is black and white. Ink on near-black for everything, hairline rules instead of fills, reverse video (ink background, ground text) for anything that is pressed, active or a key. Hue exists only where the data carries meaning: a muted green for up, a muted red for down, an amber for real warnings. Geist sets the prose; JetBrains Mono appears only for what a person types or the machine prints. Depth comes from light and tilt (a perspective stage, a spotlight, a bezel), not from shadows on content.

Behind the content runs a full-bleed ASCII trench: two ridges rendered by ASCII Magic, panned at different speeds, a band of light sweeping the near ridge, and a sparse canvas field of flickering glyphs. It steps back past the first screen.
keyCharacteristics: One palette shared with the CLI `mono` theme; the page never invents a color the app does not have.
Reverse video is the only emphasis fill: keycaps, the primary button, the current chapter key, selection.
Hairline rules and one frame language (outer radius with a hairline, 4px padding, inner radius with a stronger hairline).
Rem-scaled layout (Osmo scaling) so the composition holds its proportions between design frames.
Motion is eased with four named curves and respects reduced motion everywhere.

rules.name: The Shared Palette Rule
rules.body: The site palette and the CLI `mono` theme are one system. Ground, ink, ink-body, ink-quiet, hairline-strong, up, down and warn are the same values in both. A change goes to `packages/tui/src/theme.ts` and `site/styles.css` together, then the tour is regenerated.

rules.name: The Signal Only Rule
rules.body: Hue carries data, never decoration. Up and down mean price direction; amber means a warning. No accent color, no brand tint, no gradient fills with hue.

rules.name: The Reverse Video Rule
rules.body: Anything pressed, active, selected or a key is ink on ground inverted: ink fill, ground text. Nothing else gets a solid light fill.

rules.name: The Machine Voice Rule
rules.body: Mono is for commands, keys, source names the app prints, and cell data. Never set headings, nav or marketing sentences in mono.

rules.name: The Tight Display Rule
rules.body: Letter-spacing tightens as size grows (-0.03em at title, -0.035em at headline, -0.04em at display) and line-height drops to 1 or below; body stays at 1.5 to 1.6.

rules.name: The Flat Content Rule
rules.body: Cards, frames, tables and rules have no drop shadows. If a surface needs lifting, step the tone or draw a hairline.

rules.name: The One Lit Object Rule
rules.body: Only the stage is lit and tilted. A second tilted or glowing object would dilute it.

dos: **Do** take every color from the frontmatter tokens, and keep the site and `mono` theme values identical.
**Do** use reverse video (ink fill, ground text) for keys, the current chapter and the primary action.
**Do** keep mono for typed and printed text only, with ligatures off.
**Do** use rem for layout so the Osmo scaling holds; design both the desktop and the 390px frame.
**Do** keep controls at least 2.75rem tall (the primary button and footer X reach it on touch and phones) and keep a visible 2px ink focus ring with 3px offset.
**Do** regenerate the tour with `site-frames.mjs` whenever the app's look changes.
**Do** put provenance (a `.webp.json` sidecar) beside every shipping raster.
donts: **Don't** add hue beyond up, down and warn; no blue accent, no coral, no launchpad colors.
**Don't** use em dashes (U+2014) anywhere in copy, code comments or docs.
**Don't** put arrows or chevrons on buttons or calls to action.
**Don't** hand-draw or screenshot-edit the CLI; frames come from the app.
**Don't** present the npm or Homebrew names as live until they are published.
**Don't** put shadows on content surfaces, or tilt or glow a second object next to the stage.
